claim: The soluble isoform of leptin receptor (sOb-R) is secreted by the liver.
source: The soluble isoform of leptin receptor (sOb-R), secreted by the liver, regulates leptin bioavailability and bioactivity.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: sOb-R regulates leptin bioavailability and bioactivity.
source: The soluble isoform of leptin receptor (sOb-R), secreted by the liver, regulates leptin bioavailability and bioactivity.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: Reduced levels of sOb-R in diet-induced obesity (DIO) contribute to hyperleptinemia and leptin resistance.
source: Its reduced levels in diet-induced obesity (DIO) contribute to hyperleptinemia and leptin resistance, effects that are regulated by the endocannabinoid (eCB)/CB1R system.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The endocannabinoid (eCB)/CB1R system regulates sOb-R levels and leptin resistance.
source: Its reduced levels in diet-induced obesity (DIO) contribute to hyperleptinemia and leptin resistance, effects that are regulated by the endocannabinoid (eCB)/CB1R system.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Pharmacological activation/blockade and genetic overexpression/deletion of hepatic CB1R modulates sOb-R levels and hepatic leptin resistance.
source: Here we show that pharmacological activation/blockade and genetic overexpression/deletion of hepatic CB1R modulates sOb-R levels and hepatic leptin resistance.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Peripheral CB1R blockade failed to reverse DIO-induced reduction of sOb-R levels in mice lacking CHOP.
source: Interestingly, peripheral CB1R blockade failed to reverse DIO-induced reduction of sOb-R levels, increased fat mass and dyslipidemia, and hepatic steatosis in mice lacking C/EBP homologous protein (CHOP), whereas direct activation of CB1R in wild-type hepatocytes reduced sOb-R levels in a CHOP-dependent manner.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 4.

claim: Direct activation of CB1R in wild-type hepatocytes reduced sOb-R levels in a CHOP-dependent manner.
source: Interestingly, peripheral CB1R blockade failed to reverse DIO-induced reduction of sOb-R levels, increased fat mass and dyslipidemia, and hepatic steatosis in mice lacking C/EBP homologous protein (CHOP), whereas direct activation of CB1R in wild-type hepatocytes reduced sOb-R levels in a CHOP-dependent manner.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 5.

claim: CHOP stimulation increased sOb-R expression and release via a direct regulation of its promoter.
source: Moreover, CHOP stimulation increased sOb-R expression and release via a direct regulation of its promoter, while CHOP deletion reduced leptin sensitivity.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 6.

claim: CHOP deletion reduced leptin sensitivity.
source: Moreover, CHOP stimulation increased sOb-R expression and release via a direct regulation of its promoter, while CHOP deletion reduced leptin sensitivity.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 4.

claim: Leptin binds the leptin receptor in hypothalamic neurons to reduce food intake and increase energy expenditure.
source: It binds the leptin receptor in hypothalamic neurons to reduce food intake and increase energy expenditure in coordination with other adipokines and gastric peptides (Allison and Myers, 2014; Pan and Myers, 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Leptin stimulates the secretion of α-melanocortin stimulating hormone (α-MSH) from proopiomelanocortin (POMC) neurons at the arcuate nucleus (ARC).
source: Molecularly, leptin stimulates the secretion of α-melanocortin stimulating hormone (α-MSH) from proopiomelanocortin (POMC) neurons at the arcuate nucleus (ARC) and inhibits the secretion of the orexigenic peptides neuropeptide-Y (NPY) and Agouti-related protein (AgRP) (Flak and Myers, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Leptin inhibits the secretion of the orexigenic peptides neuropeptide-Y (NPY) and Agouti-related protein (AgRP).
source: Molecularly, leptin stimulates the secretion of α-melanocortin stimulating hormone (α-MSH) from proopiomelanocortin (POMC) neurons at the arcuate nucleus (ARC) and inhibits the secretion of the orexigenic peptides neuropeptide-Y (NPY) and Agouti-related protein (AgRP) (Flak and Myers, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Genetic leptin deficiency results in morbid obese and insulin resistance phenotypes in animals.
source: Genetic leptin deficiency or lack of functional leptin receptor results in morbid obese and insulin resistance phenotypes in animals (Lepob/ob or Leprdb/db mice, respectively) (Tartaglia et al., 1995; Zhang et al., 1994).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Lack of functional leptin receptor results in morbid obese and insulin resistance phenotypes in animals.
source: Genetic leptin deficiency or lack of functional leptin receptor results in morbid obese and insulin resistance phenotypes in animals (Lepob/ob or Leprdb/db mice, respectively) (Tartaglia et al., 1995; Zhang et al., 1994).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Congenital leptin deficiencies in humans lead to hyperphagia and early-onset obesity, which can be reversed with leptin replacement therapy.
source: In humans, congenital leptin deficiencies are rare, leading to hyperphagia and early-onset obesity, which can be reversed with a leptin replacement therapy (Mantzoros, 1999).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Most cases of obesity are characterized by hyperleptinemia, indicating that obesity is a leptin-resistant state.
source: However, most cases of obesity are characterized by hyperleptinemia, indicating that obesity is a leptin-resistant state, where leptin signaling is impaired.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: The liver is a central organ in the regulation of whole-body energy homeostasis and constitutes an important target for leptin.
source: For instance, the liver, a central organ in the regulation of whole-body energy homeostasis, constitutes an important target for leptin as it regulates hepatic gluconeogenesis and insulin sensitivity as well as lipid metabolism (Frühbeck and Nutr, 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Leptin regulates hepatic gluconeogenesis and insulin sensitivity as well as lipid metabolism.
source: For instance, the liver, a central organ in the regulation of whole-body energy homeostasis, constitutes an important target for leptin as it regulates hepatic gluconeogenesis and insulin sensitivity as well as lipid metabolism (Frühbeck and Nutr, 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Defects in leptin action in a state of hepatic leptin resistance impair hepatic function and lead to hyperglycemia, hyperinsulinemia, and dyslipidemia.
source: Therefore, defects in leptin action, which occur in a state of hepatic leptin resistance, impair hepatic function and lead to hyperglycemia, hyperinsulinemia, and dyslipidemia (Frühbeck and Nutr, 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: In humans, sOb-R is exclusively generated via proteolytic shedding of membrane-anchored isoforms.
source: In humans, sOb-R is exclusively generated via proteolytic shedding of membrane-anchored isoforms (Maamra et al., 2001), whereas in mice, it is produced by both transcription of a designated isoform (Ob-Re) and ectodomain shedding of Ob-Rb and Ob-Ra (Ge et al., 2002; Li et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: In mice, sOb-R is produced by both transcription of a designated isoform (Ob-Re) and ectodomain shedding of Ob-Rb and Ob-Ra.
source: In humans, sOb-R is exclusively generated via proteolytic shedding of membrane-anchored isoforms (Maamra et al., 2001), whereas in mice, it is produced by both transcription of a designated isoform (Ob-Re) and ectodomain shedding of Ob-Rb and Ob-Ra (Ge et al., 2002; Li et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: sOb-R is mainly produced by hepatocytes and is the main leptin-binding protein in human plasma.
source: sOb-R, mainly produced by hepatocytes, is the main leptin-binding protein in human plasma, regulating leptin's bioavailability and bioactivity (Lammert et al., 2001; Yang et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: The circulating levels of sOb-R are inversely correlated with body weight and free leptin levels.
source: In fact, studies have shown that the circulating levels of sOb-R are inversely correlated with body weight and free leptin levels (Ogier et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: sOb-R levels are increased following weight loss.
source: In addition, sOb-R levels are increased following weight loss (Laimer et al., 2002; Reinehr et al., 2005), and its overexpression in mice increases leptin sensitivity (Huang et al., 2001; Lou et al., 2010), supporting the key role of sOb-R in the development as well as the reversal of leptin resistance.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Overexpression of sOb-R in mice increases leptin sensitivity.
source: In addition, sOb-R levels are increased following weight loss (Laimer et al., 2002; Reinehr et al., 2005), and its overexpression in mice increases leptin sensitivity (Huang et al., 2001; Lou et al., 2010), supporting the key role of sOb-R in the development as well as the reversal of leptin resistance.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: The eCB/CB1R system is highly overactive during obesity.
source: The eCB/CB1R system is highly overactive during obesity (Engeli, 2008; Engeli et al., 2005; Matias et al., 2006; Monteleone et al., 2005), and both central and peripheral stimulations of this system have been suggested to contribute to the development of the metabolic syndrome, including leptin resistance (Engeli et al., 2005; Matias et al., 2008; Pagotto et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Central and peripheral stimulations of the eCB/CB1R system contribute to the development of the metabolic syndrome, including leptin resistance.
source: The eCB/CB1R system is highly overactive during obesity (Engeli, 2008; Engeli et al., 2005; Matias et al., 2006; Monteleone et al., 2005), and both central and peripheral stimulations of this system have been suggested to contribute to the development of the metabolic syndrome, including leptin resistance (Engeli et al., 2005; Matias et al., 2008; Pagotto et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Leptin's ability to regulate food intake and peripheral lipid metabolism depends upon hypothalamic CB1Rs.
source: Studies have shown that leptin's ability to regulate food intake and peripheral lipid metabolism depends upon hypothalamic CB1Rs (Buettner et al., 2008; Cardinal et al., 2014; Di Marzo et al., 2001; Jo et al., 2005; Malcher-Lopes et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: DIO-related hyperleptinemia is completely reversed by increasing leptin's renal clearance and decreasing its secretion from adipocytes through peripheral CB1R blockade.
source: By using peripherally restricted CB1R blockers, we have recently demonstrated that DIO-related hyperleptinemia is completely reversed by increasing leptin's renal clearance and decreasing its secretion from adipocytes (Tam et al., 2012; Tam et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The reversal of hypothalamic leptin resistance in obese mice treated with JD5037 is mediated via re-sensitizing the animals to endogenous leptin and re-activating POMC neurons.
source: Additionally, we have shown that the reversal of hypothalamic leptin resistance in obese mice treated with the peripherally restricted CB1R blocker, JD5037, is mediated via re-sensitizing the animals to endogenous leptin and re-activating POMC neurons (Tam et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Hypothalamic neurons, including POMC, undergo endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress during DIO, which may contribute to the development of leptin resistance.
source: Several lines of evidence suggest that hypothalamic neurons, including POMC, undergo endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress during DIO, which may contribute to the development of leptin resistance (Ozcan et al., 2009; Ramírez and Claret, 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of peripheral CB1Rs (by AM6545) reverses the high-fat diet (HFD)-induced hepatic elevation in the ER stress marker phospho-eIF2α.
source: We have previously reported that pharmacological inhibition of peripheral CB1Rs (by AM6545) reverses the high-fat diet (HFD)-induced hepatic elevation in the ER stress marker phospho-eIF2α (Tam et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: A significant reduction in serum levels of sOb-R was documented in obese mice, an effect that was ameliorated by JD5037 treatment.
source: Similar to previous findings (Mazor et al., 2018), a significant reduction in serum levels of sOb-R was documented in obese mice, an effect that was ameliorated by JD5037 treatment (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: JD5037 treatment affected the transcription and protein levels of Lepr-s (Ob-Re) isoform.
source: Measurements of the Lepr-s (Ob-Re) isoform revealed that JD5037 treatment also affected its transcription and protein levels (Figure 1C–E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1C-E.

claim: The protein expression of Ob-Rb and Ob-Ra in liver homogenates was decreased in DIO mice and normalized following JD5037 treatment.
source: Moreover, the protein expression of two additional isoforms of LEPR (Ob-Rb and Ob-Ra) in liver homogenates was also decreased in DIO mice and normalized following JD5037 treatment (Figure 1D–E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1D-E.

claim: LCB1 cKO mice gain similar weight to their wild-type littermate controls when fed with a HFD.
source: When fed with a HFD, these mice gain similar weight to their wild-type (WT) littermate controls [(Osei-Hyiaman et al., 2008) and Figure 1F]
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1F and a citation.

claim: LCB1 cKO mice are less prone to develop liver steatosis, dyslipidemia, and leptin resistance when fed with a HFD.
source: When fed with a HFD, these mice gain similar weight to their wild-type (WT) littermate controls [(Osei-Hyiaman et al., 2008) and Figure 1F]; however, they are less prone to develop liver steatosis, dyslipidemia, and leptin resistance (Osei-Hyiaman et al., 2008), making hepatic CB1R a central regulator of obesity-related liver complications.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by a citation.

claim: The liver specific deletion of CB1R was sufficient to maintain normal circulating levels of sOb-R in obese LCB1 cKO mice.
source: We were therefore not surprised to find that the liver specific deletion of CB1R was sufficient to maintain normal circulating levels of sOb-R in obese LCB1 cKO mice (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The hepatic gene and protein expression of sOb-R and the other LEPR isoforms were not affected by the HFD feeding in LCB1 cKO mice.
source: Similarly, the hepatic gene and protein expression of sOb-R and the other LEPR isoforms were not affected by the HFD feeding (Figure 1B,C and G,H), suggesting that hepatic CB1R most likely regulates sOb-R levels.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1B, C, G, H.

claim: Only obese LCB1 cKO mice remained leptin sensitive as measured by pSTAT3/STAT3 ratio in response to leptin.
source: Whereas both lean WT and LCB1 cKO mice showed elevated pSTAT3/STAT3 ratio in response to leptin (Figure 1I,J), only obese LCB1 cKO mice remained leptin sensitive (Figure 1K,L).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1I-L.

claim: LCB1 cKO mice are resistant to obesity-induced hyperleptinemia.
source: These results are in line with findings from Osei-Hyiaman and colleagues (Osei-Hyiaman et al., 2008), demonstrating that LCB1 cKO mice are resistant to obesity-induced hyperleptinemia.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by a citation.

claim: hTgCB1 cKO mice are resistant to DIO like global CB1R KO mice.
source: These mice, despite being resistance to DIO like global CB1R KO mice [(Liu et al., 2012; Tam et al., 2010) and Figure 1M], demonstrate increased circulating leptin levels when fed a HFD (Liu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1M and citations.

claim: hTgCB1 cKO mice demonstrate increased circulating leptin levels when fed a HFD.
source: These mice, despite being resistance to DIO like global CB1R KO mice [(Liu et al., 2012; Tam et al., 2010) and Figure 1M], demonstrate increased circulating leptin levels when fed a HFD (Liu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by a citation.

claim: The circulating and hepatic sOb-R levels in hTgCB1 cKO mice were decreased by 50% following 14 weeks consumption of a HFD.
source: In accordance with that, the circulating and hepatic sOb-R levels in these mice were decreased by 50% following 14 weeks consumption of a HFD (Figure 1N–Q).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1N-Q.

claim: The hepatic pSTAT3/STAT3 ratio in hTgCB1 cKO mice did not respond to exogenous leptin, suggesting reduced hepatic leptin sensitivity.
source: Moreover, the hepatic pSTAT3/STAT3 ratio did not respond to exogenous leptin, suggesting reduced hepatic leptin sensitivity (Figure 1R,S).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1R, S.

claim: Overexpression of CB1R in the liver alone compromises hepatic leptin sensitivity and recapitulates the HFD-induced downregulation of sOb-R observed in WT mice.
source: Hence, overexpression of CB1R in the liver alone compromises hepatic leptin sensitivity and recapitulates the HFD-induced downregulation of sOb-R observed in WT mice.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and is an inference from the data presented.

claim: Direct activation of CB1R with noladin ether (NE) decreased sOb-R levels in the culture media of hepatocytes.
source: We analyzed both culture media and cell lysates and found that, similar to obesity, direct activation of CB1R also decreased sOb-R levels in the culture media.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2.

claim: CB1R-mediated reduction in ObR levels was completely reversed by blocking CB1R using JD5037.
source: This CB1R-mediated reduction in ObR levels was completely reversed by blocking CB1R using JD5037 (Figure 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Treatment of HFD-fed mice with JD5037 normalized p-eIF2α levels.
source: Similar to our previous findings (Tam et al., 2010), treatment of HFD-fed mice with JD5037 normalized p-eIF2α levels (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B), suggesting relieved ER stress following CB1R blockade.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B and a citation.

claim: A comparable ratio of hepatic phospho-to-total eIF2α ratio was documented in lean and obese LCB1 cKO mice.
source: In agreement with these findings, a comparable ratio of hepatic phospho-to-total eIF2α ratio was documented in lean and obese LCB1 cKO mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: Both the hepatic mRNA (Ddit3) and protein levels of CHOP were downregulated in obese WT mice.
source: Measuring the expression levels of the ER stress marker C/EBP homologous protein (CHOP) revealed surprising findings, since both the hepatic mRNA (Ddit3) and protein levels of CHOP were downregulated in obese WT mice, despite the suggested ER stress.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3A-D.

claim: CHOP expression levels were reversed above control levels by JD5037 in obese WT mice.
source: Its expression levels were reversed above control levels by JD5037, and remained comparable between lean and obese LCB1 cKO mice (Figure 3A–D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3A-D.

claim: CHOP levels remained comparable between lean and obese LCB1 cKO mice.
source: Its expression levels were reversed above control levels by JD5037, and remained comparable between lean and obese LCB1 cKO mice (Figure 3A–D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3A-D.

claim: CHOP levels were positively correlated with the levels of sOb-R in both experimental paradigms.
source: In fact, CHOP levels were positively correlated with the levels of sOb-R in both our experimental paradigms, leading us to hypothesize that CHOP may directly be involved in the regulation of sOb-R.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and is an inference from the data presented.

claim: JD5037 was almost equieffective in reducing body weight and fat mass in both obese WT and CHOP KO mouse strains.
source: Whereas JD5037 was almost equieffective in reducing body weight and fat mass in both obese mouse strains (Figure 3E–G), it improved plasma cholesterol levels as well as hepatic steatosis in WT mice only (Figure 3H–J).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3E-G.

claim: JD5037 improved plasma cholesterol levels as well as hepatic steatosis in WT mice only, not in CHOP KO mice.
source: Whereas JD5037 was almost equieffective in reducing body weight and fat mass in both obese mouse strains (Figure 3E–G), it improved plasma cholesterol levels as well as hepatic steatosis in WT mice only (Figure 3H–J).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3H-J.

claim: The basal levels of AEA and 2-AG were markedly higher in CHOP KO mice than in the WT control group.
source: Strikingly, we found that the basal levels of AEA and 2-AG were markedly higher in CHOP KO mice than in the WT control group.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: The increased eCB levels in CHOP KO mice remained unchanged following a consumption of HFD as well as JD5037 treatment.
source: Moreover, the increased eCB levels in CHOP KO mice remained unchanged following a consumption of HFD as well as JD5037 treatment (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: CHOP may play a pivotal role in modulating hepatic eCB 'tone'.
source: Overall, these data indicate that CHOP may play a pivotal role in modulating hepatic eCB 'tone', and that it is required for the beneficial effects of CB1R blockade on dyslipidemia and hepatic steatosis.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and is an inference from the data presented.

claim: CHOP is required for the beneficial effects of CB1R blockade on dyslipidemia and hepatic steatosis.
source: Overall, these data indicate that CHOP may play a pivotal role in modulating hepatic eCB 'tone', and that it is required for the beneficial effects of CB1R blockade on dyslipidemia and hepatic steatosis.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and is an inference from the data presented.

claim: Circulating levels of sOb-R were comparable in lean and obese mice in WT and CHOP KO strains.
source: Measuring the effect of CHOP deficiency on sOb-R levels revealed comparable circulating levels of sOb-R in lean and obese mice in the two mouse strains.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: JD5037 failed to restore sOb-R levels in CHOP KO mice.
source: However, JD5037 failed to restore sOb-R levels in CHOP KO mice (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Lepr-s mRNA expression and sOb-R protein content in the livers of CHOP KO mice showed reduced baseline levels compared to WT.
source: The assessment of Lepr-s mRNA expression and sOb-R protein content in the livers of both strains documented reduced baseline levels in CHOP KO mice, compared to WT, which still remained low following HFD consumption and/or JD5037 treatment (Figure 4B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 4B,C.

claim: The HFD-induced hyperleptinemia was vastly reduced by JD5037 treatment in WT mice, whereas it was only partially ameliorated by JD5037 in CHOP KO animals.
source: The HFD-induced hyperleptinemia was vastly reduced by JD5037 treatment in WT mice, whereas it was only partially ameliorated by JD5037 in CHOP KO animals (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The hepatic pSTAT3/STAT3 ratio in lean CHOP KO mice was comparable before and after stimulation with exogenous leptin.
source: Interestingly, the hepatic pSTAT3/STAT3 ratio in lean CHOP KO mice was comparable before and after stimulation with exogenous leptin (Figure 4G,H).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 4G,H.

claim: The regulation of sOb-R levels is CHOP-dependent.
source: Taken together, our data suggest that the regulation of sOb-R levels is CHOP-dependent.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and is an inference from the data presented.

claim: Regulation of the soluble isoform by CHOP can consequently affect circulating leptin levels and hepatic leptin sensitivity, possibly, in a CB1R-dependent manner.
source: In addition, regulation of the soluble isoform by CHOP can consequently affect circulating leptin levels and hepatic leptin sensitivity, possibly, in a CB1R-dependent manner.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and is an inference from the data presented.

claim: A direct activation of CB1R downregulated CHOP mRNA expression.
source: Similar to a HFD consumption in mice (Figure 3A), a direct activation of CB1R downregulated CHOP mRNA expression (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The expression of Ppp1r15a, a downstream target of CHOP, was reduced in NE-treated WT hepatocytes, and remained unchanged in CHOP KO cells.
source: We validated this by measuring the expression levels of Ppp1r15a, a downstream target of CHOP (Hu et al., 2018), and found that its expression was also reduced in NE-treated WT hepatocytes, and remained unchanged in CHOP KO cells (Figure 5B), suggesting that CB1R activation in fact leads to reduced CHOP expression and activity.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5B and a citation.

claim: CB1R activation leads to reduced CHOP expression and activity.
source: We validated this by measuring the expression levels of Ppp1r15a, a downstream target of CHOP (Hu et al., 2018), and found that its expression was also reduced in NE-treated WT hepatocytes, and remained unchanged in CHOP KO cells (Figure 5B), suggesting that CB1R activation in fact leads to reduced CHOP expression and activity.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and is an inference from the data presented.

claim: NE was able to reduce sOb-R levels in WT hepatocytes, but had the opposite effect in CHOP KO hepatocytes.
source: Whereas NE was able to reduce sOb-R levels in WT hepatocytes, it had the opposite effect in CHOP KO hepatocytes, suggesting that CB1R may regulate sOb-R levels in other mechanisms independently of CHOP (Figure 5C–E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5C-E.

claim: CB1R may regulate sOb-R levels in other mechanisms independently of CHOP.
source: Whereas NE was able to reduce sOb-R levels in WT hepatocytes, it had the opposite effect in CHOP KO hepatocytes, suggesting that CB1R may regulate sOb-R levels in other mechanisms independently of CHOP (Figure 5C–E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and is speculation based on the data presented.

claim: Treatment with tunicamycin (TM) for 6 hr led to a robust expression of CHOP mRNA and protein in WT cells.
source: Treatment with TM for 6 hr led to an expected and robust expression of CHOP mRNA and protein in WT cells (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 6A,B.

claim: TM treatment was accompanied with elevated mRNA expression levels of Lepr-s as well as secreted levels of sOb-R into the culture media in WT, but not CHOP KO hepatocytes.
source: Importantly, this was accompanied with elevated mRNA expression levels of Lepr-s as well as secreted levels of sOb-R into the culture media in WT, but not CHOP KO hepatocytes (Figure 6C–E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 6C-E.

claim: Increased levels of sOb-R in culture media were documented when CHOP was exogenously overexpressed in WT hepatocytes.
source: Increased levels of sOb-R in culture media were also documented when we exogenously overexpressed myc-tagged CHOP in WT hepatocytes (Figure 6F,G), supporting a direct role for CHOP in Lepr gene regulation.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 6F,G.

claim: CHOP expression and luciferase activity in transfected cells was induced using TM.
source: By using a luciferase reporter assay, in which the −650 to +850 (relative to transcription start site) region of the LEPR promoter was cloned into firefly luciferase expressing vector, we found that CHOP expression and luciferase activity in transfected cells was induced using TM (Figure 6H), while CB1R activation using NE (which downregulates CHOP expression as seen in Figure 5A) had an opposite effect in WT, but not in CHOP KO cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 6H.

claim: CB1R activation using NE had an opposite effect on luciferase activity in WT, but not in CHOP KO cells.
source: By using a luciferase reporter assay, in which the −650 to +850 (relative to transcription start site) region of the LEPR promoter was cloned into firefly luciferase expressing vector, we found that CHOP expression and luciferase activity in transfected cells was induced using TM (Figure 6H), while CB1R activation using NE (which downregulates CHOP expression as seen in Figure 5A) had an opposite effect in WT, but not in CHOP KO cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 6H.

claim: There was a twofold increase in the recovery of the qPCR product amplified with a primer set flanking the putative CHOP binding site in cells treated with TM.
source: As seen in the CHOP precipitates (Figure 6I), there was a twofold increase in the recovery of the qPCR product amplified with a primer set flanking the putative CHOP binding site, in cells that were treated with TM.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 6I.

claim: CHOP is able to occupy the Lepr promoter and directly regulate sOb-R levels in response to HFD consumption and/or CB1R activation.
source: Taken together, our data suggests that CHOP is able to occupy the Lepr promoter and directly regulate sOb-R levels in response to HFD consumption and/or CB1R activation.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and is an inference from the data presented.

claim: HFD induces the mRNA and protein expression levels of hepatic Trib3.
source: Our in vivo data indicate that HFD induces the mRNA and protein expression levels of hepatic Trib3, and that treatment with JD5037 restores these levels.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-E.

claim: Treatment with JD5037 restores HFD-induced hepatic Trib3 levels.
source: Our in vivo data indicate that HFD induces the mRNA and protein expression levels of hepatic Trib3, and that treatment with JD5037 restores these levels.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-E.

claim: In CHOP KO mice, Trib3 levels did not change in response to HFD nor JD5037 treatment.
